<result>## Report — Slot Machine cabinet

**Model:** `primitive:cube:15` (lane-slot_machine), 6 primitive faces confirmed at `look`, matched brief exactly before starting.

**Build:** Scaled the bootstrap cube to the cabinet envelope first (0.65 × 1.75 × 0.6 m, grounded y=0), then box-modeled the whole thing from that single cube — no `add`-ed parts, so there's nothing to weld/junction-repair; the model is one continuous manifold shell by construction.

- **cabinetBase** — flat front, y 0–1.0 (pedestal/lower cabinet)
- **controlDeck.cap / controlDeck.wall** — extruded 0.09 m off the front, top edge pulled back 0.06 m to create the sloped button shelf (bottom sticks out 0.09 m, top 0.03 m)
- **screen.cap / screen.wall** — `inset` recess into the front face (0.025 m deep, 72%×80% of the bezel band). The negative-distance inset produced inverted winding on the wall ring (8 tris, 24% of mesh unreachable by the 42-direction visibility audit) — caught it with `select-audit kind:unreachable`, `flip`ped the region, re-audited to 0/0.
- **marqueeHeader.cap / marqueeHeader.wall** — extruded 0.035 m proud at the top for the header/sign box
- **leverMount.wall → leverArm.wall → leverKnob.cap/.wall** — one-sided appendage box-modeled off the right flank (`right` face carved to a 0.30×0.12 m patch via `basic-cut`, extruded out as mount boss → shaft → knob, shaft angled downward by moving the cap vertices, knob bulged with a uniform scale). Mirror stayed off throughout, per instructions.

**Final state:** 39 authored regions, 78 triangles, `unnamed: 0`, `0 intersecting / 0 unreachable`. Bbox ≈ x[-0.325, 0.606], y[0, 1.75], z[-0.39, 0.3] m (envelope core is the requested 0.65×1.75×0.6, lever assembly and control-deck slope are the only envelope excursions, as intended).

**Refusals / adaptations:**
- `basic-cut`'s `offset` parameter did not have a stable top-vs-bottom convention across different sub-face selections — I stopped guessing and instead verified every cut's actual position empirically via `inside:box` probes after each call, occasionally undoing and retrying with a corrected offset. Slower but reliable; worth flagging since the skill doc doesn't document this ambiguity.
- `inset` with a negative distance silently produced inverted-normal wall geometry (caught via the unreachable-geometry audit, fixed with `flip` — documenting this since a future inset-for-recess call should expect to check/flip).
- **Anomaly worth reporting, not silently worked around:** one `scale-uniform 1.35` call returned `{"ok":false,"reason":"uniform scale rejected — needs a finite nonzero factor and an in-scope vertex/edge/face selection"}` even though the selection was valid (10 faces, just confirmed), and the very next `look` showed the mesh *had* actually scaled (bboxes moved, geometry still 0/0 clean). Generation counter doesn't increment on transform ops so I can't confirm from that signal alone. I did not fight it further — the result was geometrically sane so I kept it and moved on to the `action scale` JSON form for anything else, but this looks like a real reporting bug in `scale-uniform` (mutates while claiming rejection) worth someone checking in `seatApi.ts`.
- `semantic-status` refused at the end: `"the UV/paint focus bridge belongs to the visible ModelView; semantic-status cannot target a background model (target model primitive:cube:15, active primitive:cube:10)"` — another lane's model is currently the visible tab. Per the skill, save's own `ok:true` already re-reads the written RJMD and would have failed/rolled back on any name drop, so semantic persistence is validated by the save postcondition even though the three-way `semantic-status` diagnostic couldn't run. I didn't force a tab switch to another lane's active session.

`save` returned `ok:true`. Claim dismissed (`primitive:cube:15`).</result>
